text:
mira: Heads up — the Python quickstart in README still shows the old curl + Authorization header example; customers hitting auth errors when they copy/paste the snippet with the new hosted token format. Repro: set REDWOOD_API_KEY and run the snippet, you get 401.

alex: Can you paste the exact snippet and error? I can take a look.

mira: Yep. Current README has: 
```bash
export API_KEY=sk-old-format
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
```
Error returned: 
```json
{ \"error\": \"invalid_token\", \"message\": \"token format not recognized\" }
```

sam: Ah this is the token format change we rolled out last quarter. The docs should say to use REDWOOD_HOSTED_TOKEN and the header name is `Redwood-Api-Key` (we also pushed an official SDK call example).

alex: Good catch. We should replace the curl example and add the SDK snippet + note about the retry semantics. Quickstart should show both minimal curl and python SDK.

mira: Proposed python SDK snippet to replace it: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_HOSTED_TOKEN"))
resp = client.generate(\"Hello world!\")
print(resp.text)
```
Also add a short note: \"If you see intermittent 429s, SDK will retry once by default; set client.retries=3 for longer flakiness windows.\"

jen: I'll open a docs PR. Do we want to keep the old `Authorization: Bearer` example but marked deprecated, or remove it entirely?

sam: Mark deprecated with a one-line callout + link to migration guide. Some customers still have tokens in the old format and need the upgrade path.

jen: OK. I'll do: replace curl with updated header and env var, add python + node SDK examples, add note about retries and how to configure backoff. Assigning to me.

docs-bot: Reminder: docs PRs need the 'docs' label and a changelog entry. See https://redwood.internal/docs-style/style-guide#breaking-changes :link: 

alex: Thanks jen — can you include an automated snippet test? We had too many regressions from copy/paste snippets. A single CI job that runs quickstart examples would prevent this.

jen: Yep, will add a tiny GH Action that runs the curl + python example against staging tokens. I'll include creds in secrets and a skip-for-local flag.

mira: Amazing — thanks. After PR lands, can we add a small note in onboarding emails to current users to regenerate tokens? Some will keep using the curl example if they don't see the README change.

sam: I'll follow up with growth to include it.

jen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423 — added updates + CI snippet test. cc @mira @alex

mira: Verified the updated snippet on staging — works. Closing out my internal bug. :tada:
